q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
NVIDIA is scheduled to report Q2 FY2027 earnings on **Wednesday, August 26, 2026**. Today is August 20, 2026. This means **6 days** remain until the earnings release and forward guidance announcement.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA's own guidance issued on May 20, 2026 projected Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, translating to a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

Wall Street consensus as of August 12, 2026 sits at approximately **$91.9 billion**, which falls comfortably within NVIDIA's guided range.

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 will be **near the upper end of its previous guidance range or slightly above it**, around $91.0-$92.0 billion, given:
- Q1 FY2027 actual results of $81.6 billion exceeded guidance by ~$2 billion (~2.5% beat)
- Wall Street consensus tracking at $91.9 billion (slightly above the $91.0B midpoint)
- Strong execution pattern suggests NVIDIA may guide conservatively and beat
- No indication of major supply disruptions or demand deterioration

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro deterioration**: Weakness in enterprise spending or AI capex slowdown
- **China restrictions tightening**: Further limitations on China revenue (though this is already excluded)
- **Geopolitical escalation**: Additional export controls or licensing restrictions
- **Competitive pressure**: Gains by AMD or other competitors reducing TAM
- **Inventory correction**: Data center customers pulling back on orders
- **Weaker-than-expected demand**: Evidence of AI investment pullback

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Strong execution continuation**: Following Q1's $2B beat pattern
- **Accelerating demand**: Data center expansion exceeding expectations
- **AI capex acceleration**: Stronger-than-anticipated enterprise AI spending
- **Market share gains**: NVIDIA capturing larger share of GPU market
- **H100/H200 ramp**: Successful product transition driving higher ASPs
- **Supply meeting demand**: Manufacturing able to meet strong customer orders
- **China revenue inclusion**: Unlikely but would be a major upside driver

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides **direct, explicit guidance**: NVIDIA issued formal guidance on May 20, 2026 of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** for Q2 FY2027, with a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**.

Additionally, Q1 FY2027 actual results of $81.6 billion **exceeded guidance by ~$2 billion**, suggesting NVIDIA tends to guide conservatively.

Wall Street consensus of $91.9 billion (as of August 12, 2026) suggests modest upside to the midpoint of NVIDIA's range.

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

Given that we have only 6 days until the earnings release:
- NVIDIA's guidance is legally binding and highly constrained at this point
- The company rarely changes guidance materially between issuance and earnings
- Q1's pattern of beating by ~2% suggests Q2 guidance could similarly come in slightly above the $91.0B midpoint
- Wall Street consensus at $91.9B represents the market's best estimate of actual results
- The range $89.2B-$92.8B should contain most outcomes (~95% confidence)

The forward guidance (not actual results) should land in NVIDIA's stated range with high probability, likely toward the upper end given the Q1 beat pattern.

For the guidance itself (not actual results reported on Aug 26), I estimate:
- 10th percentile: $89.8 billion (near lower bound, accounting for downside tail risks)
- 50th percentile: $91.5 billion (slightly above midpoint, consistent with conservative guidance pattern)
- 90th percentile: $93.5 billion (upper end with upside scenario)

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The company's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projected Q2 FY2027 revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, meaning a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This outlook explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), a stance that has been in place for the past year due to U.S. licensing requirements for chips sold into China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, according to Yahoo! Finance data compiled as of August 12, 2026, have a consensus estimate of approximately $91.9 billion for Q2 FY2027 revenue [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's guidance range [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its own guidance by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 is considered a key indicator, with current consensus at $103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).
